sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Alphalogic Industries is a small engineered-storage supplier with improving margins but declining latest revenue and a large financial-asset allocation. FY26 sales fell 27.73% to ₹45.0764 crore while PAT rose 83.98% to ₹5.3869 crore. Interest income contributed ₹2.063 crore, 28.62% of pretax profit. The low debt headline is incomplete: ₹11.6036 crore is lent on an unsecured, on-demand basis and the AU-bank fixed deposit secures an overdraft. At the secondary-provider 19 October close of ₹138, the current-issued/no-future-exercise five-year reference base return is −1.27%; matched remaining-warrant conversion gives −3.39%. The no-exercise bull barely meets 15% at 15.02%, but matched conversion reduces that bull to 12.29%. This is a valuation and capital-allocation watchlist, not a bargain established by past growth or low borrowings.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Issuer: Alphalogic Industries Limited, formerly Alphalogic Trademart, incorporated 22 September 2020 and renamed 28 January 2022; BSE SME 543937, ALPHAIND, ISIN INE 0 NZF 01019. It is not the separately listed Alphalogic Techsys. The June 2023 prospectus identifies the correct issuer despite copied parent-company wording on parts of the investor portal. September 29 conversion increased issued shares to 10,519,200; the official security-master capital remains stale and is superseded by the allotment filing. Techsys's unchanged 5,214,528 shares fell to 49.57% ownership through dilution, ending subsidiary status without a disposal. Research cutoff 20 October 2026. Audited annual statements and allotment evidence support Medium historical confidence; future orders, loan realization and conditional trading estimates remain uncertain.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 6, CASH 4, BAL 7, EXEC 5 and EARN 5 produce BQS 5.34 and Growth Quality 6.25. R 1, D 2, P 2 and L 1 produce IAS =0.25×5.34 +0.35×1 +0.20×2 +0.10×2 +0.10×1 =2.385. No score changes follow the warrant correction: the current-issued/no-future-exercise base return of −1.27% remains 16.27 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, still R 1. The matched exercise base is −3.39% and also R 1. No missing-factor reweighting or automatic cash-quality cap applies: CASH 4 does not meet the persistent≤3 cap rule. All gates are Conditional, not failed. Reported loans and related transactions warrant scrutiny but do not themselves establish dishonesty or critical financial unreliability. The prior fully diluted/no-cash result is retained only as an asymmetric conservative bound, not the central forecast.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The business designs, fabricates and installs industrial racking, shelving, compactors, mezzanine systems and related storage products. Customer economics depend on usable space, load capacity and installation schedules, not software-like recurring subscriptions. The prospectus says capacity depends on workforce and orders rather than a fixed machinery-output measure, so a standardized utilization percentage should not be invented. FY 26 management describes additional leased shed space ahead of demand. Current website references to dark stores, quick-commerce customers and installations are issuer marketing, not independently audited contracted backlog. Earlier history included paddy trading and other services, limiting a simplistic claim that all historical growth represents the same manufacturing franchise.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Customization, engineering, safe load design, references and installation capability can protect relationships, but awards and certification do not demonstrate sustained pricing power. The prospectus disclosed FY 23 top-five customers at 71.37% and top-ten at 85.58%, with top-ten suppliers at 92.09%. These dated figures establish historical concentration, not current exact percentages. Large orders can make half-year revenue volatile. Godrej Storage Solutions is a substantive operating competitor, offering selective, drive-in, shuttle and mobile pallet systems with manufacturing and engineering capabilities. Its broader operations are not a directly transplantable listed-company valuation. No peer P/E is used; the model applies explicit analyst multiples to Alphalogic's own operating earnings, with competitive-margin sensitivities.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Full-year operating revenue in FY 22–FY 26 was₹7.8433/18.0185/47.5351/62.3682/45.0764 crore, a 54.83% four-year CAGR. FY 21 revenue₹3.2233 crore belongs to a partial first year after September 2020 incorporation and is not used to manufacture a five-year comparable CAGR. The business mix also evolved from trading toward engineered storage. Latest sales fell 27.73%, while management attributes the decline to order timing and customer-project deferrals. That explanation is a claim to test against subsequent invoices, not a verified current backlog. The forecast base begins with₹50 crore FY 27 revenue and 15% initial growth thereafter, slowing toward 10%; the bull requires substantially more successful order conversion. No economic benefit is assigned merely because an announced customer is in a fast-growing end market.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Manufacturing assets are small: physical PPE₹1.6303 crore, with a separate₹0.2974 crore right-of-use asset. FY 26 physical capex₹0.7229 crore is modest, but low fixed assets do not imply all cash is freely distributable. Deposits₹9.1209 crore and loans₹11.6036 crore together absorb₹20.7245 crore, over half total assets. A calculated operating-capital proxy excludes those financial assets and gives average capital near₹8.0634 crore; operating NOPAT near₹4.0731 crore implies approximately 50.5% return. This small-denominator operating return must not be applied to the entire balance sheet. Total deployed capital earns a mix of operating margins and lower-yield financial returns. Incremental operating capital actually fell, so an infinite or mechanically exceptional incremental ROIC is not reported. CAP 6 reflects useful operating economics tempered by allocation and concentration risk.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
FY 26's managing-director letter acknowledges the revenue decline and attributes improved margins to selective orders and material-cost discipline. Financial audit and internal-control evidence reviewed do not establish a critical qualification. CARO states on-demand loans had no overdue amounts, repayments were demanded and received during the year, overdue loans were not rolled over, and sections 185/186 were complied with. These are meaningful counterweights to a blanket diversion allegation, not a guarantee of future collection.

Related activity remains material: Enlight Metals Private Limited sales₹7.6175 crore, purchases₹8.5322 crore; Techsys deputation expenses₹0.8728 crore; gross related lending₹15 crore, within₹24.19 crore total loan grants. Closing related loans are ₹3.5 crore and the net Techsys receivable is₹3.4199 crore. Managerial remuneration to Montubhai and Krina Gandhi totals₹0.18 crore. The broad note about related balances being unsecured/interest-free is not used to erase separately disclosed loan interest. Arm's-length assertions are management disclosures rather than independent transaction pricing verification. The September dilution is not characterized as promoter selling. Continued parent-linked funding and deployment decisions deserve monitoring even after formal subsidiary status ends.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY 24–FY 26 CFO was−₹2.9863/+3.4555/+4.3859 crore against PAT₹2.3492/2.9280/5.3869 crore. Three-year conversion is 45.53%, despite stronger recent cash. FY 26 inventory absorbed₹0.4791 crore, receivables released₹0.6994 crore and other current assets absorbed₹1.3488 crore. Other current liabilities supplied₹2.2508 crore, chiefly customer advances rising from₹0.3714 crore to₹2.6940 crore. Customer funding is useful but can reverse as projects execute.

Reported CFO excludes financial interest income, which appears in investing cash flow. FY 26 net loans given consumed₹2.7857 crore, new noncurrent deposits₹9.1207 crore, and current-deposit release supplied₹5.2632 crore. Consequently positive operating cash did not become a large cash balance. Total cash₹0.02 crore includes₹0.0066 crore escrow. The AU deposit₹9.0602 crore secures the ₹0.8528 crore overdraft; it is not assumed freely available at entry. Other FD₹0.0607 crore is also kept separate from immediate operating cash. Net income tax payable is only ₹0.0399 crore after offsetting₹1.7811 crore advance tax/TDS against₹1.8210 crore provision, preventing double counting. Financial income₹2.063 crore must not be valued at an operating multiple and then have the underlying deposits/loans added again.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The model separates operating enterprise value from financial assets. Annual FY27–FY31 forecasts plus a final FY32 April–October stub end 19 October 2031, exactly five years after the dated entry. The full FY27 bridge starts with March balances and includes unreported pre-entry changes; it is not a verified October bank statement. Base annual revenue is ₹50/57.5/66.125/74.06/81.466/89.6126 crore, EBITDA margin 12% before cash rent, working capital 20% of sales and capex 2%. Cash lease payments replace the right-of-use depreciation/lease-debt approach, avoiding a second lease liability deduction. Terminal replacement depreciation is normalized rather than allowed to vanish.

The loan book is not assumed collected to fund growth before exit. It earns 10% modeled interest in the base, while deposits earn 7.1%. Income is taxed, retained cash supports operations, and financial principal is credited once at terminal realization subject to loss sensitivities. Base debt interest 11% includes half-year new draws, with hypothetical debt limited to ₹3 crore and 2 times EBITDA; equity gaps would be funded at 30% below entry plus 5% issue costs. The base requires no new debt or equity. Only the confirmed ₹0.693 crore September receipt is already in the opening bridge.

The central reference uses 1.05192 crore currently issued shares and assumes no further exercise or unreceived exercise cash. A separate literal conversion path assumes all 1,470,000 remaining warrants exercise on 31 March 2027, adding ₹3.087 crore cash and 0.147 crore shares together. Original deposits are already in the balance sheet and are not added again. Conversion cash enters after FY27 operating cash and interest, before closing debt repayment; it is not available throughout that year. Exercise is optional and the reference is not a probability assertion that deep-in-the-money warrants will lapse. The previous 1.19892 crore denominator without its exercise cash survives only as a deliberately asymmetric conservative bound.

Operating-NOPAT exit multiples remain 10/14/18 for bear/base/bull and 7 severe. Current-issued/no-exercise results are base ₹129.44/−1.27% IRR, bear ₹44.79/−20.15%, bull ₹277.82/15.02% and severe ₹15.22/−35.66%. Base 15% hurdle entry is about ₹64.35. Matching conversion cash and shares gives base ₹116.14/−3.39%, bear ₹42.01/−21.17%, bull ₹246.33/12.29% and severe ₹13.79/−36.91%. The asymmetric fully diluted/no-cash bound remains ₹113.57/−3.82%; it is not called the base.

On the current-issued/no-exercise reference, 50% loan impairment gives ₹121.63/−2.49%, complete loan loss ₹113.81/−3.78%, 10% operating margin ₹106.15/−5.11%, and 30% WC ₹120.68/−2.65%. The important conclusion is unchanged: neither literal base path meets the 15% hurdle, and weak liquidity compounds implementation risk. The no-exercise bull's narrow hurdle clearance is not robust to actual warrant conversion.

The original 1 January 2026 allotment filing confirms an 18-month exercise window and forfeiture of the initial deposit if unexercised. The alternative 31 March 2027 conversion date is within that window. It is an analyst timing assumption, not a disclosed investor exercise instruction. [WARRANT_ORIG, ALLOT]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Orders may remain deferred while the leased shed and staff still cost money. Related-party and other on-demand borrowers may not repay when cash is needed, and deposit collateral may require bank settlement before release. Customer advances can run down just as inventory or receivables increase. Bear assumptions combine slower revenue,8.5% EBITDA margin,25% working capital and 50% loss of the loan book. Severe assumptions allow full loan loss,20% deposit-value stress,1.5 crore operating-asset impairment and 5% margins; residual model value is not a liquidation guarantee. Financial-asset impairments reduce recoverable assets and future interest, not a fabricated immediate cash payment. Operating impairments reduce opening recoverable working capital and are funded once through the closing-stock bridge. No assumed tax shield offsets losses. Unavailable financing or worse recovery could push actual equity value below the modeled severe outcome, including zero.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At ₹138, fivefold appreciation requires ₹690 and tenfold ₹1,380, corresponding to about 37.97% and 58.49% annual returns over five years. The current-issued/no-exercise bull reaches ₹277.82, only 2.01 times entry, despite revenue ₹140.94 crore, 15% margins, 17% WC and an 18 times operating-NOPAT multiple. The matched-conversion bull reaches ₹246.33, 1.79 times entry. A 5× outcome would require equity value about ₹725.82 crore on current issued shares or ₹827.25 crore on fully converted shares, before any additional funding dilution. Both are far above modeled bull operating-plus-financial-asset values. A speculative rerating or much larger successfully funded business would be necessary; current evidence does not justify treating either as a base. The old fully diluted/no-cash calculation is only a conservative bound, not a literal conversion scenario.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track the next sales release against management's deferred-order explanation, especially margin and customer-advance movement. Review the unsecured loan register, related borrower balances, actual interest receipts and whether surplus is redeployed into more lending. Verify deposit pledge release and lender balances before calling them free cash. Reconcile each residual warrant exercise with cash received and the share denominator; do not count the original 25% deposit twice. Follow related-party approvals, Techsys deputation and changing managerial roles. For implementation, obtain current BSE restrictions, lot and live depth; an old closing price and sparse secondary trades do not establish an executable position size.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Valuation-constrained, capital-allocation-sensitive watchlist. BQS 5.34, Growth Quality 6.25 and conditional IAS 2.385 do not support extrapolating the past growth story at the dated price. Liquidity is particularly weak: the matched secondary source contains 10 of 20 and 19 of 60 reference sessions. Observed-only 20-session turnover bounds average ₹4.7508–5.0644 lakh and median ₹1.6620–1.6650 lakh; the 60-session median bounds are ₹1.6620–1.6692 lakh. Even the optimistic observed median implies roughly 60 trading days for a ₹5 lakh exit at 5% participation. Missing dates are not automatically zero-filled, and low/high×volume is not actual traded value. The 600-share master lot costs ₹82,800 at ₹138; latest volume was 1,200 shares. No bonus/split crosses the reviewed window: the last disclosed 1:1 bonus was December 2023, whereas September 2026 warrant conversion is an issuance, not a price-adjusting split. Conditional L 1 does not claim verified live spread, regulatory clearance or a trading prohibition.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The issuer's FY 26 and FY 25 reports, June 2023 prospectus and September 29 allotment filing establish financial history, capital actions and risk scope. Some documents were obtained from mirrors of the actual signed issuer filings after exchange download errors; identity and document dates were checked. Security-master lot information is distinguished from its stale share count. The secondary price/volume record is explicitly bounded and not promoted to primary traded-value evidence. Remaining uncertainties are present order conversion, loan recovery/timing, future related deployment, deposit-release conditions, exact October cash, residual warrant exercise and live BSE execution. The annual model makes these assumptions visible rather than disguising them inside a P/E target. A material adverse correction undermining the audited loan/asset balances would require revisiting G 2 and possibly making IAS not scoreable.

assumption_basis: Base revenue recovers to ₹50 crore in FY27 from ₹45.0764 crore, then grows at approximately 15%, 15%, 12%, 10% and 10%. The latest annual decline and unverified backlog make this an analyst scenario, not management guidance achieved.

Base EBITDA margin of 12% before cash rent is near FY26 core reported operating EBITDA margin of 12.7%. Bear 8.5%, bull 15% and severe 5% test mix and competition. The model deducts ₹0.1716 crore annual cash lease payments and physical-asset depreciation, not ROU depreciation plus another lease-debt deduction.

Opening operating working capital excludes ₹11.6036 crore loans, ₹9.1209 crore deposits and ₹0.3799 crore accrued financial interest. Ordinary supplier advances, GST balances, customer advances and creditors remain operating. Net current tax ₹0.0399 crore is settled once; the accrued interest is collected once.

Opening cash excludes ₹0.0066 crore escrow and adds only the confirmed ₹0.693 crore September warrant-conversion balance. A ₹0.5 crore operating reserve is retained outside distributable cash. The original ₹1.26 crore warrant deposit is already in March balances and is not added again.

The AU-bank FD is pledged for overdraft. No early deposit or loan principal release funds base growth; both remain financial assets earning modeled income and are credited once at terminal realization. Loan yield is 10% in base versus FY26 loan interest ₹1.4696 crore on changing balances; FD yield 7.1% follows the note. Principal realization remains conditional, with 50% and 100% loan-loss tests and a separate severe deposit stress.

Financial interest is excluded from operating terminal NOPAT. Annual interest after tax contributes retained cash, while principal is counted once as a terminal asset; no operating multiple is applied to that interest and then added again to principal. Surplus operating cash is not assigned an additional yield, conservatively.

Base capex is 2% of revenue, bull 2.5%, with ten-year blended new-asset depreciation and half-year convention. Terminal normalized depreciation is at least recurring capex rather than zero when original assets are old. These are analyst maintenance/replacement estimates, not a disclosed engineering plan.

Bank interest is 11% on opening debt plus half-year new borrowing, solved iteratively. Base analytical debt limit is the lower of ₹3 crore and twice EBITDA, not a sanctioned facility. Residual gaps require equity at 30% below entry and 5% fees. Base financing needs are zero; bear/severe equity is explicitly hypothetical.

The central scenarios use 1.05192 crore currently issued shares and no unreceived warrant cash. A matched conversion alternative assumes all 1,470,000 outstanding warrants exercise on 31 March 2027, adding both ₹3.087 crore cash and 0.147 crore shares. The initial deposit is already in March 2026 balances and is not added again. Conversion cash enters after FY27 operating cash and interest, before closing repayment; it is not treated as available throughout FY27. The old 1.19892 crore denominator without exercise cash is retained only as a deliberately asymmetric conservative bound, not a literal central path.

Loan and deposit impairments reduce recoverable financial assets and future yield, without an invented immediate cash payment or tax shield. Operating-asset impairments reduce recoverable opening working capital and are funded once through closing working capital. The model uses 25% tax on positive pre-impairment profit.

Analyst operating-NOPAT exit multiples are 10, 14 and 18 times, and 7 severe; no peer quote is transplanted. No dividend is assumed. Exact terminal date is 19 October 2031, with a final fractional-year stub after FY31. The FY27 bridge includes unreported pre-entry movements rather than claiming current October cash is observed.

Original warrants were allotted on 1 January 2026 with an 18-month exercise window. The matched alternative date31 March2027 is inside that contractual window; it is not a forecast instruction from the warrant holders.
